newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil closes lower, backwardation eases.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil closes lower, backwardation eases.

text.p: IPE gas oil closed lower on Friday as the front month backwardation came under heavy pressure from a lack of prompt demand on physical spot markets in northwest Europe, traders said.
Trading volumes on both gas oil and Brent were thin.
Jan gas oil closed $2.75 down at $215 a tonne, while the Jan/Feb spread shed $2.00 to close at just +$1.50.
"The front spread has come right off because of lack of demand on the physical market," a broker said.
"We're due for a lot of cold weather in the States, but (the effects) just haven't kicked in over here yet."
Slack European markets and stronger demand in the U.S. have allowed Russian gas oil cargoes to start moving across the Atlantic.

Independent U.S. forecaster Weather Services Corp said a cold front would push across the eastern part of the United States -- a key heating oil market -- towards the middle of next week, bringing cold weather in its wake.
IPE Brent was trading 20 cents down at $23.78 a barrel at 1735 GMT off a session low of $23.70.
Failing to draw any inspiration from trade on NYMEX, London dealers went in for some modest profit taking ahead of the Christmas holiday, brokers said.
"It's really thin and volatile. There isn't really any strength behind the market whatever way it moves," said one.
